authority: uvp-core uvp-ir::canonical_stringify (serde_json integer number identity; float-form literals rejected at the authority, bug_audit #15)
consumers: uvp-protocol packages/compiler canonical.ts must reproduce pass cases byte-for-byte and reject the expectReject cases with an equivalent single rejection face
rules: The canonical hash-preimage vocabulary is closed over integers: number literals without '.' or 'e' (u64/i64) canonicalize bare, without a decimal point.

Float-form number literals are rejected outright (bug_audit #15): any f64 payload — integral floats (100.0), fractions (1.5), exponent spellings (1e2, 2.5e-8, 1e300), and negative zero (-0.0) — fails loudly at the authoritative canonicalizer, listing the offending token. Cross-language float formatting (ryu vs JS Number->String) carries no byte-for-byte alignment obligation; the single rejection face lives in the Rust authority.
Object keys sort by code point; arrays keep order.

cases.name: integer token stays a bare integer
u64 beyond double precision stays an integer
keys sort by code point over integers
exponent spelling is a float and is rejected
negative zero is a float and is rejected
small scientific float nested in an array is rejected
large scientific float nested deep in an object is rejected
